description: SOC-thermal Nernst + Arrhenius-R model for ICFB stack. Temperature range 15-65 degC. Extends F1a with temperature-dependent resistance and Nernst thermal factor.

unit.name: Generic 40-cell ICFB stack, 500 cm2 electrode area
unit.source: Shibata, S., Sumino, M. P. (1988). J. Power Sources 25, 177; Hruska, L. W., Savinell, R. F. (1981). J. Electrochem. Soc. 128, 18; Zeng, Y. K. et al. (2015). J. Power Sources 278, 294

E0.note: Standard cell potential Fe3+/Fe2+ vs Cr3+/Cr2+ (0.77 - (-0.41) = 1.18 V at 25 degC)

R_cell_ohm_cm2_ref.note: Area-specific resistance at T_ref; ICFB uses Nafion-style membrane, typical 4 Ohm.cm2 at 25 degC

n.note: Single electron transfer: Fe3++e-<->Fe2+ and Cr3++e-<->Cr2+

pump_loss_coefficient.note: Pump parasitic power ~ k_pump * I^2 (approximate scaling with flow rate)

E_a.note: Activation energy for membrane/electrode resistance; Cr kinetics are sluggish, typical E_a 18-25 kJ/mol
E_a.source: Zeng et al. (2015) J. Power Sources 278, 294; Hruska & Savinell (1981) J. Electrochem. Soc. 128, 18

dOCV_dT.note: Temperature coefficient of standard potential. For Fe3+/Fe2+ + Cr3+/Cr2+: dE0/dT = -delta_S/(n*F). delta_S for Fe3+/Fe2+ ~ -134 J/mol/K, Cr3+/Cr2+ ~ 20 J/mol/K -> net ~ -154 J/mol/K -> dE0/dT ~ -0.00160 V/K for Fe half, -0.00021 V/K for Cr half; combined ~-0.0004 V/K at cell level. Operationally confirmed warmer = lower E0 for Fe/Cr redox couple.
dOCV_dT.source: Atkins Physical Chemistry (2014) thermodynamic data; Shibata & Sumino (1988) J. Power Sources 25, 177

T_min.note: 15 degC lower limit (Cr kinetics unacceptably slow below 10-15 degC)

T_max.note: 65 degC upper limit (ICFB tolerates elevated temperature; electrolyte stable to ~65 degC)
